name: Mary Bliss
bio: E. P. Warren's first cousin, to whom he had dedicated his privately printed fairy tale The Prince Who Did Not Exist (1900), and who married his partner John Marshall on 5 November 1907. Fothergill's memoir has her arriving at Lewes House and courting 'Ned and Marshall, either of which she was well prepared to marry', and thinking naively that the marriage would bind Marshall closer to Warren. She died at the Villa Buonvisi, Bagni di Lucca, in 1925; all three of them share the tomb there.
bio_note: Her birth year is not recorded by Sox, who calls her 'Ned's spinster cousin' and 'a middle-aged cousin' at the time she came to Lewes House, before 1901. Promoted from the context_engagement on marshall.json, 2026-08-05; the source moved with her unchanged, verified at the printed page. Sox's own verdict on the union: 'Neither love nor sex had anything to do with the union of Mary and John Marshall, but she was an extremely beneficial help-mate in his collecting at the Metropolitan Museum.'
